title: Choose Shammy's visual world
question: The roll assigned Truck-Art Night Shift: the notch as a hand-painted Indian truck tailboard at night. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Truck-Art Night Shift
options.lineage: Hand-painted Indian highway truck art: 'Horn OK Please', nazar eyes, painted borders
options.thesis: The notch is a truck's painted tailboard at night: the pet is its nazar eyes, each activity rides in its own painted colour band.
materials: enamel sign paint on a night-indigo ground
options.viewport: Indigo-black notch; the open view's cards are painted panels, each framed by a 2px pinstripe in its activity colour; numerals in a sign-painter's condensed caps; the action circle is the truck's 'OK' roundel.
options.risk: Tips into kitsch if the paint goes beyond borders, numerals and the eyes; the working screen must stay quiet.

raised.raise: One reserved colour (marigold) marks only the single live activity; every other band steps down to its muted tone.
A changed item (new notification, finished timer) holds its colour band lit until you've seen it, then settles.
The big numerals sit on a variable weight axis that breathes with the music level and thickens as a timer nears zero.
Each card owns its hue as a full-strength field when it opens to detail, not a tinted chip.

options.label: Sticker-Bombed Lid
options.lineage: Student and developer laptop lids covered in die-cut vinyl stickers
options.thesis: Every activity is a die-cut sticker slapped onto the black notch: thick white keyline, a slight tilt, peeling and re-sticking as things change.
materials: die-cut vinyl with white keylines and a holographic foil
options.viewport: Black notch; cards are stickers at 1–2° tilts with white keylines; the pet is a round sticker that peels a corner when it moves; the action circle is a small round sticker.
options.risk: Familiar sticker-UI trope among design lovers; tilts must stay subtle or the grid feels messy.

options.label: Focus Wall
options.lineage: Streaming catalogue rows where the focused tile grows
options.thesis: The open notch is one row of artwork-first tiles: the one under your pointer grows and explains itself while the rest dim.
materials: full-bleed artwork and data as the only colour
options.viewport: A single horizontal rail of fixed-ratio tiles; the focused one scales up with its title and one line; neighbours slide aside and dim.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and reads instantly as a working shelf; loses on audience identity (it's Netflix, not Shammy).
options.risk: Generic media-app feel; the pet gets lost among artwork.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.lineage: Dark-first developer tools: graphite panels, hairline seams, syntax colours
options.thesis: A precise graphite panel system with hairline seams; syntax-derived colours carry state only.
options.viewport: Persistent tiled panels with small-caps headers and monospaced figures; one accent for the primary action.
options.case: Developers recognise it at once and it's very clear; it's also closest to what we already have, so it adds little identity.
options.risk: This is near the category default (dark + accents); Shammy would look like every dev tool.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain colours underneath, the active course in purple on top.
options.viewport: Contour-textured ground with a purple course line linking activities.
options.case: Fuses poorly: neither the audience nor a notch reads as terrain.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the single active item.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.lineage: Boxed-software manuals with coloured tab dividers
options.thesis: Each section a full-strength colour board with clear acetate leaves above.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail with the current section's board behind content.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a reference manual is the opposite of a glanceable notch.
options.kept: A section owns its hue at full strength, never a tint.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.lineage: Airport boarding passes and departure boards
options.thesis: Activities ranked like departures; changes flash and hold.
options.viewport: A ranked board of today's activities with a pass-style detail.
options.case: Fuses partly: good for calendar, wrong for music and the pet.
options.kept: A changed item holds its alert colour until noticed.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms morph live along an axis.
options.viewport: Giant numerals whose weight moves with a slider.
options.case: Fuses poorly as a whole world, but the live axis idea is strong.
options.risk: A type showcase, not a notch.
options.kept: Numerals on a live variable axis that responds to what's happening.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Apple's Dynamic Island and the Mac notch apps, executed impeccably: pure black, system font, one accent per activity.
canonCard.viewport: Black island with live activities and widget cards, exactly as Apple would.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every notch app by design.
